paper_title: Getting More Out of Black Hole Superradiance: a Statistically Rigorous Approach to Ultralight Boson Constraints from Black Hole Spin Measurements
coupling_convention: f_a in GeV (from QCD axion relation Eq.12) vs m_a in eV; QCD-axion-line intersection of the 2D (mu, f^-1) exclusion for M33 X-7
notes: Black hole superradiance constraints on ultralight boson mass mu and self-interaction/decay constant f (f^-1). Primary result is a 2D exclusion region in the (mu, f^-1 [GeV^-1]) plane (Fig. 4) for two BHs (stellar-mass M33 X-7 and SMBH IRAS 09149-6206), reported at 95% credible region. These contours are only available as plots and cannot be read numerically here. The cleanest text-based limit is the QCD-axion excluded mass band for M33 X-7: 0.6 peV < mu < 3 peV, which I converted to f_a using Eq.(12) mu = 5.691 neV x (1e15 GeV / f_a), giving f_a ~ 1.9e18-9.5e18 GeV. IRAS 09149-6206 constrains much lighter bosons around mu ~ 3e-19 eV (SMBH). This is an astrophysical bound, so no DM density assumption. Coupling type is genuinely ambiguous between AxionMass (f_a-m_a plane) and a decay-constant f^-1 [GeV^-1] representation; confidence kept low.
